headline: Mirrors don't create images—they redirect light that's already there
universal_truth: What we see in others is often a reflection of ourselves
fun_facts: Mirrors don't flip left and right—they flip front and back; your brain interprets this as a left-right swap
Ancient mirrors were made of polished bronze, silver, or obsidian—glass mirrors came later
Mirrors reflect about 85-95% of light; the 'perfect mirror' doesn't exist
discussion_questions: What do you see when you look in a mirror—really?
Who in your life serves as a 'mirror' for you?
How might we be mirrors for others without realizing it?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You've looked in mirrors thousands of times, but have you ever considered: you've never actually seen your own face—only light bouncing off it. The person you see in the mirror isn't you. It's photons that touched you and then touched your eyes.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Here's a mystery most people get wrong: mirrors don't flip left and right. Your left hand is still on the left side of the reflection. So why does text appear backwards? What's really happening?

options.text: Mirrors flip front and back—not left and right
options.response: Exactly. The mirror reverses the axis perpendicular to its surface. Your brain interprets this as a lateral flip.

options.text: Mirrors flip left and right because of how our eyes process images
options.response: It feels that way, but the physics are different...

q1.title: Reflection Physics
q1.script: When light hits a smooth surface, it bounces off at the same angle it arrived. A mirror's surface is smooth at the atomic level, so light rays stay organized—preserving the image. Rough surfaces scatter light randomly, which is why walls don't reflect images.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "Reflection Physics"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: The Front-Back Flip
q2.script: Hold a book up to a mirror. The text is backwards—but your left hand is still on the left. What's actually reversed is front and back. The book's front now faces you in the reflection. Your mind interprets this as a left-right flip, but it isn't.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Ancient Mirrors
q3.script: Before glass mirrors, people used polished obsidian, bronze, and silver. The oldest manufactured mirrors are 8,000 years old. Humans have always sought to see themselves—reflection is ancient technology serving an ancient need.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom—fitting for Valentine's Day: other people are our mirrors. What annoys us in them often reflects something in ourselves. What we admire in them often reveals what we aspire to. Choose your mirrors wisely.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 45. Tomorrow, we'll discover how sound bounces back as echoes. Until then, look in a mirror—and consider what you're really seeing.
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Human Mirrors - See Your Reflection
growTrack.learning_objective: Recognize how others reflect aspects of yourself
growTrack.activity: Think of someone who annoys you and someone you admire. What quality bothers you about the first? What do you admire in the second? Consider: do these qualities exist in you too? Others often mirror our hidden selves.
